We are already seeing the impacts of a very strong El Niño this winter, and we have much work and little time to ready ourselves.  Join me, @AsmMarcBerman, Supervisor @Ray_Mueller_, and Supervisor @margaretabekoga for a virtual El Niño Preparedness Town Hall to hear directly from state and local emergency officials about how to keep your family and community safe. 

RSVP now: https://t.co/zUybKO1gyF

For 15 years, Andrea Mackenzie has championed conservation across Santa Clara Valley, helping protect Coyote Valley and expand access to open space for thousands of families.

Last week, I had the honor of recognizing her remarkable leadership and lasting contributions to our community. Congratulations, Andrea!

America must keep its promise to the Afghans who risked their lives alongside our troops.

On Monday night, @RepJasonCrow and I filed a discharge petition to force a vote on our Afghan TPS Act, which would protect eligible Afghans from deportation back to Taliban-controlled Afghanistan.

Thank you to the 114 colleagues of both parties who have already signed on. We won’t stop pushing until we reach 218 signatures!
Stay away from the water this weekend! There is a High Surf Warning today through Sunday. Please avoid beaches to keep yourself and our first responders safe. https://t.co/YjAfqa3ZHu

Veterans forced to medically retire because of combat injuries often lose a dollar of retirement pay for every dollar they receive in VA disability compensation.

Today, I voted to pass the Major Richard Star Act to end this “wounded veteran tax” and ensure that our wounded warriors receive both benefits in full.

They’ve already sacrificed for our country, so they shouldn’t have to sacrifice the benefits they earned. Now the Senate must act.

Heavy rain, strong winds, and dangerous surf are headed to the Bay Area, with waves reaching up to 30 feet along our coast.

Please prepare now. Check your flood risk, avoid dangerous surf, and sign up for local emergency alerts to stay informed: https://t.co/LNJM2KF9Lc https://t.co/IQdGgW87FJ

This Veterans Day, we thank every veteran for your service and sacrifice.

When those who served our country return home, we must uphold our solemn promise: to deliver the care and support they deserve.

That means giving Palo Alto VA staff the resources to care for veterans, keeping the Moffett Field Commissary open for affordable groceries, and enacting the Major Richard Star Act, so that combat-injured veterans can receive both their full military retirement pay and VA disability compensation.

The 119th Congress has been one of the least productive in history— and history will not forgive congressional inaction on AI safety.

I joined @karaswisher and @RepCasar to discuss what it will take for Congress to catch up next year.

Check it out: https://t.co/obvfRLeTpc

To prepare for El Niño, we can use a Sharpie, or we can use science. 

Thankfully, San Mateo County is preparing for the storm season with cutting-edge scientific research and data analytics.  I recently spoke at their event to introduce the new Atmospheric River Emergency System (ARES).  

A partnership between Scripps scientists and the County’s Emergency Management Department, ARES will improve visibility of looming atmospheric rivers often missed by National Weather Service satellite tracking, to provide earlier warnings. 

I urge everyone to join me in taking steps today to prepare for the upcoming storm season: clean your gutters, establish a family emergency plan, pack a go bag, and sign up for emergency alerts at https://t.co/X5Ju0knAP3  San Mateo County, or https://t.co/Fcm4SRixdB in Santa Clara County. Don’t wait for the storm to start preparing!

On Día de Muertos, we honor the lives and cherished memories of our loved ones who have passed on. 

We recently lost my Mom, Laura, after a long bout with illness. She was born Laura Aceves, the daughter of an Irish immigrant and Mexican-American mechanic who endured childhood poverty, losing her own mother to cancer as an adolescent, and an unstable home. She eventually left home to board with the Sisters of Notre Dame as a teen, and she was smart and resourceful.   Her grades won her admission to Stanford, but she couldn’t afford the tuition, so she completed her training to start a nursing career. Having five children eventually persuaded her to rethink her career plans, and she and my Dad enjoyed nearly 67 years of marriage, adventurous travel, three grandchildren, and two (exuberant) great-grandchildren.  

My Mom developed an inspiring resilience, relying on humor to endure life’s hardships, and built lifelong friendships with her magnetic laughter. She repeatedly challenged me and my siblings not to allow our setbacks to swallow our happiness, and helped us brush ourselves off–with a hug–after every fall.  

Wishing a wonderful Día de Muertos to all who celebrate.

Veterans forced to medically retire because of combat injuries often lose a dollar of retirement pay for every dollar they receive in VA disability compensation.

Today, I voted to pass the Major Richard Star Act to end this “wounded veteran tax” and ensure that our wounded warriors receive both benefits in full.

They’ve already sacrificed for our country, so they shouldn’t have to sacrifice the benefits they earned. Now the Senate must act.

post.text:
This Veterans Day, we thank every veteran for your service and sacrifice.

When those who served our country return home, we must uphold our solemn promise: to deliver the care and support they deserve.

That means giving Palo Alto VA staff the resources to care for veterans, keeping the Moffett Field Commissary open for affordable groceries, and enacting the Major Richard Star Act, so that combat-injured veterans can receive both their full military retirement pay and VA disability compensation.
